title: CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE, AXONAL, TYPE 2A1
alt_titles: CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE, AXONAL, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT, TYPE 2A1
HEREDITARY MOTOR AND SENSORY NEUROPATHY IIA1

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 (CMT2A1) is caused by mutation in the KIF1B gene (605995) on chromosome 1p36.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 (CMT2A1) is caused by mutation in the KIF1B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract shows that CMT2A is caused by KIF1B mutation. The draft's name 'CMT2A1' is just standard nomenclature for this disease.

checks.claim: The KIF1B gene is located on chromosome 1p36.
checks.evidence_quote: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A was previously mapped to an interval containing KIF1B.
checks.explanation: The abstract doesn't name 1p36, but a gene's chromosomal location counts as standard nomenclature. The abstract does say the CMT2A interval contains KIF1B.

paragraphs.text: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 is an autosomal dominant axonal (non-demyelinating) peripheral neuropathy that causes progressive muscle weakness (Xu et al., 2018). CMT is divided into 2 main types: demyelinating CMT1, with nerve conduction velocities below 38 m/s, and axonal CMT2, with conduction velocities above 38 m/s, which are in the normal range (Xu et al., 2018). CMT2A is genetically heterogeneous. CMT2A1 is caused by mutation in the KIF1B gene (Zhao et al., 2001), and CMT2A2, the most common known form, is caused by mutation in the MFN2 gene (Xu et al., 2018).

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 is an autosomal dominant peripheral neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: diagnosed with autosomal-dominant CMT2 disease
checks.explanation: Table 2 also lists inheritance as autosomal dominant.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 is an axonal (non-demyelinating) peripheral neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Demyelinating CMT1 has a nerve conduction velocity <38 m/s, and axonal CMT2 has nerve conduction velocities >38 m/s.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 causes progressive muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: suffering from CMT2A symptoms including progressive muscle weakness and slight central nervous system defects

checks.claim: CMT is divided into 2 main types: demyelinating CMT1 and axonal CMT2.
checks.evidence_quote: CMT disease is divided into two main types on the basis of electrophysiological properties and neuropathology: CMT1 and CMT2.

checks.claim: Demyelinating CMT1 has nerve conduction velocities below 38 m/s.
checks.evidence_quote: Demyelinating CMT1 has a nerve conduction velocity <38 m/s

checks.claim: Axonal CMT2 has nerve conduction velocities above 38 m/s, which are in the normal range.
checks.evidence_quote: axonal CMT2 has nerve conduction velocities >38 m/s
checks.explanation: Normal range also stated in Discussion: 'CMT2 is defined as axonal hereditary neuropathy with a normal range of axon conduction speeds'.

checks.claim: CMT2A is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Mitofusin 2 (MFN2) mutations, which impair mitochondrial fusion and ER–mitochondria tethering, are responsible for the most common known axonal form of CMT2A2
checks.explanation: Paper distinguishes CMT2A1 (KIF1B) and CMT2A2 (MFN2), implying genetic heterogeneity.

checks.claim: CMT2A1 is caused by mutation in the KIF1B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states that CMT2A patients carry a KIF1B mutation.

checks.claim: CMT2A2 is caused by mutation in the MFN2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mitofusin 2 (MFN2) mutations, which impair mitochondrial fusion and ER–mitochondria tethering, are responsible for the most common known axonal form of CMT2A2

checks.claim: CMT2A2 is the most common known form of CMT2A.
checks.evidence_quote: are responsible for the most common known axonal form of CMT2A2
checks.explanation: Paper says 'most common known axonal form'; phrasing ambiguous rather than explicitly most common form of CMT2A.

paragraphs.text: Saito et al. (1997) reported that in their CMT2 patients, tendon reflexes were preserved in the upper extremities but reduced or absent in the lower extremities.

checks.claim: In the CMT2 patients reported by Saito et al. (1997), tendon reflexes were preserved in the upper extremities.
checks.evidence_quote: tendon reflexes preserved in upper extremities but reduced or absent in lower extremities
checks.explanation: The abstract says this about the affected members of the two CMT2A families.

checks.claim: In the CMT2 patients reported by Saito et al. (1997), tendon reflexes were reduced or absent in the lower extremities.
checks.evidence_quote: tendon reflexes preserved in upper extremities but reduced or absent in lower extremities

paragraphs.text: Xu et al. (2018) described a patient with a progressive, symmetric, length-dependent, sensorimotor, predominantly axonal polyneuropathy.

checks.claim: Xu et al. (2018) described a CMT2A1 patient with a progressive, symmetric, length-dependent polyneuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Progressive, symmetric, length dependent, sensory motor, predominantly axonal polyneuropathy with intermittent cranial nerve involvement

checks.claim: The polyneuropathy in the CMT2A1 patient described by Xu et al. (2018) was sensorimotor.
checks.evidence_quote: Progressive, symmetric, length dependent, sensory motor, predominantly axonal polyneuropathy

checks.claim: The polyneuropathy in the CMT2A1 patient described by Xu et al. (2018) was predominantly axonal.
checks.evidence_quote: Progressive, symmetric, length dependent, sensory motor, predominantly axonal polyneuropathy

paragraphs.text: Xu et al. (2018) reported autosomal dominant inheritance of CMT2A1.

checks.claim: CMT2A1 shows autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: KIF1B | CHR1: 10387567 | Y1087C | Heterozygote | Autosomal dominant
checks.explanation: Table 2 and Patient 2 diagnosis indicate autosomal dominant inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) carried out pedigree linkage analysis in 6 large autosomal dominant CMT2 families. Three of the families showed linkage, and the authors mapped the CMT2A locus to the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 1.

checks.claim: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) carried out pedigree linkage analysis in 6 large autosomal dominant CMT2 families.
checks.evidence_quote: We have performed pedigree linkage analysis in six large autosomal dominant CMT2 families

checks.claim: Three of the 6 autosomal dominant CMT2 families studied by Ben Othmane et al. (1993) showed linkage to chromosome 1p.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families, DUK662, DUK1241, and 1523 gave posterior probabilities of 1.0, 0.98, and 0.88 of being of the linked type.
checks.explanation: The abstract names three families as the linked type to the chromosome 1p markers, and its multipoint analysis treats them as the 'linked' families.

checks.claim: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) mapped the CMT2A locus to the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 1.
checks.evidence_quote: have demonstrated linkage and heterogeneity to a series of microsatellites (D1S160, D1S170, D1S244, D1S228 and D1S199) in the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 1
checks.explanation: The abstract places CMT2A in the distal region of 1p, between D1S244 and D1S228.

paragraphs.text: Saito et al. (1997) carried out linkage analysis in 2 Japanese CMT2 families using markers flanking the CMT2A, CMT2B, and CMT2D loci. They obtained a highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 at D1S244 on chromosome 1p35-p36.

checks.claim: Saito et al. (1997) carried out linkage analysis in 2 Japanese CMT2 families.
checks.evidence_quote: we performed linkage analysis of two Japanese CMT2 families using markers flanking the CMT2A, CMT2B, and CMT2D loci.

checks.claim: Saito et al. (1997) used markers flanking the CMT2A, CMT2B, and CMT2D loci for linkage analysis in 2 Japanese CMT2 families.
checks.evidence_quote: we performed linkage analysis of two Japanese CMT2 families using markers flanking the CMT2A, CMT2B, and CMT2D loci.

checks.claim: In 2 Japanese CMT2 families, Saito et al. (1997) obtained a highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 at marker D1S244.
checks.evidence_quote: The highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 was obtained at D1S244.
checks.explanation: The lod score and marker match the abstract.

checks.claim: Marker D1S244, which gave the highest lod score in the 2 Japanese CMT2 families studied by Saito et al. (1997), is located on chromosome 1p35-p36.
checks.evidence_quote: at least three loci identified: CMT2A (1p35-36), CMT2B (3q13-22)
checks.explanation: The abstract places the CMT2A locus at 1p35-36 and links the families to it via D1S244, but it never gives D1S244's own band. The location is implied, not stated.

paragraphs.text: Xu et al. (2018) noted that Zuchner et al. (2004) had found MFN2 point mutations in several CMT2A pedigrees. The MFN2 gene lies in the same genomic interval as KIF1B. CMT2A caused by MFN2 mutation is designated CMT2A2 and is the most common known axonal form. Although a KIF1B mutation was the first to be identified in a pedigree with CMT2A, only a few pedigrees with KIF1B-beta mutations causing CMT2A1 have been reported (Xu et al., 2018).

checks.claim: MFN2 point mutations have been found in several CMT2A pedigrees.
checks.evidence_quote: There are several pedigrees of CMT2A with MFN2 point mutations (Züchner et al., 2004; Kijima et al., 2005; Lawson et al., 2005; Baloh et al., 2007)

checks.claim: The MFN2 gene lies in the same genomic interval as the KIF1B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Although a KIF1B mutation in the same genomic interval was the first identified in a pedigree with CMT2A
checks.explanation: Paper states KIF1B is in the same genomic interval as MFN2.

checks.claim: CMT2A caused by MFN2 mutation is designated CMT2A2.
checks.evidence_quote: Mitofusin 2 (MFN2) mutations, which impair mitochondrial fusion and ER–mitochondria tethering, are responsible for the most common known axonal form of CMT2A2

checks.claim: CMT2A2, caused by MFN2 mutation, is the most common known axonal form of CMT.
checks.evidence_quote: are responsible for the most common known axonal form of CMT2A2
checks.explanation: Paper's wording is ambiguous; it does not clearly say most common axonal form of CMT overall.

checks.claim: A KIF1B mutation was the first mutation to be identified in a pedigree with CMT2A.
checks.evidence_quote: Although a KIF1B mutation in the same genomic interval was the first identified in a pedigree with CMT2A

checks.claim: Only a few pedigrees with KIF1B-beta mutations causing CMT2A1 have been reported.
checks.evidence_quote: only a few pedigrees with KIF1Bβ mutation for CMT2A1 have been reported until recently

paragraphs.text: Zhao et al. (2001) showed that patients with CMT2A carried a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene, which encodes a kinesin superfamily motor protein.

checks.claim: Zhao et al. (2001) showed that patients with CMT2A carried a loss-of-function mutation in the KIF1B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.

checks.claim: The KIF1B mutation in CMT2A patients reported by Zhao et al. (2001) lies in the motor domain of KIF1B.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the mutation is in the motor domain.

checks.claim: The KIF1B gene encodes a kinesin superfamily motor protein.
checks.evidence_quote: The kinesin superfamily motor protein KIF1B has been shown to transport mitochondria.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes KIF1B as a kinesin superfamily motor protein.

paragraphs.text: Zhao et al. (2001) found that Kif1b knockout mice died at birth from nervous system defects. Heterozygous Kif1b mice had a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors and suffered from progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.

checks.claim: Zhao et al. (2001) found that Kif1b knockout mice died at birth.
checks.evidence_quote: KIF1B knockout mice die at birth from apnea due to nervous system defects.

checks.claim: Kif1b knockout mice died at birth from nervous system defects.
checks.evidence_quote: KIF1B knockout mice die at birth from apnea due to nervous system defects.
checks.explanation: The abstract gives the cause of death as nervous system defects (via apnea).

checks.claim: Heterozygous Kif1b mice had a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors.
checks.evidence_quote: The KIF1B heterozygotes have a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors

checks.claim: Heterozygous Kif1b mice suffered from progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.
checks.evidence_quote: suffer from progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.

Tendon reflexes reduced or absent in lower extremities, preserved in upper extremities
Nerve conduction velocities in the normal range (>38 m/s)
